scope: Owner-requested analysis and ground-up redesign of the three weakest Opera careers (Pop Star, Ballerina, Racer), citing published console, PC and mobile games and child-development research, delivered as a written Codex handoff. It records the owner's verdict (ODR-MINIGAME-REBUILD-20261017), opens MA-OPERA-014 and moves MA-OPERA-005 to CONFIRMED_OPEN on owner evidence. It benefits the child by replacing generic chores with one real skill per job: a music-timed drum echo, a danced ballet and a lane race. No game script, scene, asset, audio or workflow is changed. Revision 2 (2026-10-18) records the owner's answers to the five design questions (all defaults: ODR-POPSTAR-CORE-20261018, ODR-POPSTAR-SONG-20261018, ODR-POPSTAR-BAND-20261018, ODR-BALLET-CONCEPT-20261018, ODR-RACER-VIEW-20261018) in the register, the packet, MA-OPERA-014 and target notes under DL-INT-08 and DL-INT-10, and follows the owner's instruction to merge into dev after green CI.
finding_scope: MA-OPERA-014 is opened CONFIRMED_OPEN P1 from the owner's verdict plus static code anchors. MA-OPERA-005 moves FIXED_PENDING_VERIFICATION to CONFIRMED_OPEN because the owner gate for the current Ballerina recital failed; its rebuild is owned by MA-OPERA-014. Related findings MA-OPERA-003, MA-OPERA-006, MA-OPERA-010, MA-PLAY-004, MA-PLAY-005, MA-VIS-008 and MA-TOUCH-004 are cited, not changed.
